Cache dependency downloads

Pattern: P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (dependency_cache)

When is cache dependency downloads applicable?

Assess cache dependency downloads for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Repeated dependency fetching is measurable; Cache inputs include lockfile and environment

Contraindications: Mutable or untrusted cached content; An equivalent cache already exists

Method: Choose dependency download state rather than unchecked build outputs; Keep installation and all required tests

name: Road Runner CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "master", "main" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "master", "main" ]

  build:

    steps:
    - name: Checkout repo

    - name: Build with Gradle

    - name: Store test reports
      if: failure()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: Test reports
        path: |
          **/build/reports/
          **/build/test-results/

  push:

    - ct-scenario/**
permissions:
  contents: read

  probe:
    name: cell-${{ matrix.cell }}

    steps:
    - name: Controlled workload
      shell: bash
      run: "if [[ \"$CELL\" == \"fail\" && \"$MESSAGE\" == *\"[ct-fail]\"* ]]; then\n\
        \  sleep 20\n  exit 1\nfi\nsleep 90\nprintf \"healthy cell completed\\n\"\n"
      env:
        CELL: ${{ matrix.cell }}
        MESSAGE: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 3
      matrix:
        cell:
        - fail
        - worker-a
        - worker-b

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check

        : "suppressed"})

        action": "run"})

        \ "failure" else 0

        \ >= settings["pause_after_failures"]:

    \

def policy(pattern,\
        \ optimized=False):

        \   "P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY": {"order": "priority_with_aging" if optimized\

        : optimized,

        \    }

name: CloudTune controlled scenario

"""Deterministic service-policy\
        \ replays, also executed inside the hosted CI fixture.

All times and outcomes\

Only previously\
        \ observed outcomes are exposed to a scheduling/selection policy.

\
        import json
import os
import statistics


PATTERNS = {
    "P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE"\
        , "P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE", "P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST",
    "P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY"\
        , "P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT", "P-LIT-DURATION-PREDICTION",
}


def policy(pattern,\
        \ optimized=False):
    values = {
        "P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE": {"\
        pause_after_failures": 2 if optimized else 0,
                         \
        \       "notify_on_pause": optimized, "recovery": "explicit_owner_reset"\
        },
        "P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE": {"suppress_unchanged_inputs": optimized,
\
        \                                "meaningful_inputs": ["user_source",\
        \ "external_dependency"]},
        "P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST": {"order"\
        : "previous_failure_ancestors_first" if optimized else "declared",
 \
        \                                   "cancel_other_jobs": False},
     \
        \   "P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY": {"order": "priority_with_aging" if optimized\
        \ else "fifo", "max_wait": 12},
        "P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT": {"skip_docs_after_observed_success"\
        : optimized,
                               "always_build": ["source"\
        , "lockfile", "setup"]},
        "P-LIT-DURATION-PREDICTION": {"predictor"\
        : "past_feature_mean" if optimized else "past_global_mean",
        \
        \                             "initial_estimate": 20, "train_count": 6},
\
        \    }
    return values[pattern]


def dataset(pattern, repeat):
  \
        \  """Three reproducible workloads; repeat changes durations, never visibility\
        \ rules."""
    if repeat not in (1, 2, 3):
        raise ValueError("\
        Replay repeat must be 1, 2 or 3")
    scale = repeat
    if pattern ==\
        \ "P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE":
        return [{"id": i, "kind": kind, "\
        outcome": outcome, "duration": 5 * scale}
                for i, (kind,\
        \ outcome) in enumerate([
                    ("scheduled", "failure"\
        ), ("scheduled", "failure"), ("scheduled", "failure"),
         \
        \           ("scheduled", "failure"), ("owner_reset", None), ("scheduled"\
        , "success"),
                    ("scheduled", "failure"), ("scheduled"\
        , "success"),
                    ("scheduled", "failure"), ("scheduled"\
        , "success")])]
    if pattern == "P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE":
        return\
        \ [{"id": i, "kind": kind, "duration": 5 * scale} for i, kind in enumerate([
\
        \            "tick", "tick", "generated_commit", "tick", "external_dependency"\
        , "tick",
            "tick", "user_source", "tick", "tick"])]
\
        \    if pattern == "P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST":
        jobs = [{"id": "\
        lint", "needs": [], "duration": 30 * scale},
                {"id"\
        : "compile", "needs": [], "duration": 10 * scale},
               \
        \ {"id": "test", "needs": ["compile"], "duration": 5 * scale},
\
        \                {"id": "package", "needs": ["test"], "duration"\
        : 3 * scale}]
        return {"previous_failures": ["test"], "jobs"\
        : jobs,
                "cases": [{"id": "fails_again", "failure"\
        : "test"},
                          {"id": "recovered", "failure"\
        : None},
                          {"id": "artifact_dependency", "failure"\
        : None}]}
    if pattern == "P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY":
        return {"\
        no_contention": [{"id": "a", "arrival": 0, "duration": 2, "priority"\
        : 1},

        \ "duration": 2, "priority": 5}],
                "contended": [{"\
        id": "blocker", "arrival": 0, "duration": 8, "priority": 0},
  \
        \                            {"id": "old", "arrival": 1, "duration"\
        : 6, "priority": 0},

        , "arrival": 1, "duration": 6, "priority": 0},

        \           {"id": "urgent", "arrival": 2, "duration": 1, "priority"\
        : 10},

        : 9 + i, "duration": 3, "priority": 9}
                             \
        \   for i in range(6)]]}
    if pattern == "P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT":
    \
        \    return [{"id": i, "change": change, "outcome": outcome, "duration"\
        : 5 * scale,
                 "failure_cause": "external_setup_failure"\
        \ if i == 2 else "build_failure" if outcome == "failure" else None}
\
        \                for i, (change, outcome) in enumerate([
               \
        \     ("source", "success"), ("docs", "success"), ("docs", "failure"\
        ),
                    ("lockfile", "failure"), ("docs", "success"\
        ), ("setup", "success"),

        \ ("source", "failure")])]

        :

        \ * scale}

        \                  ("small", 10), ("large", 90), ("small", 12), ("\

        , 12), ("large", 93),

        \ 90)])]
    raise ValueError("Unsupported replay pattern: " + pattern)
\
        

def schedule_failures(data, settings):
    failures, paused, trace, notifications\
        \ = 0, False, [], []
    for row in data:
        if row["kind"] == "\
        owner_reset":
            failures, paused = 0, False
            trace.append({"\
        id": row["id"], "action": "owner_reset"})
            continue
 \
        \       if paused:
            trace.append({"id": row["id"], "action"\
        : "suppressed"})
            continue
        trace.append({**row, "\
        action": "run"})
        failures = failures + 1 if row["outcome"] ==\
        \ "failure" else 0
        if settings["pause_after_failures"] and failures\
        \ >= settings["pause_after_failures"]:
            paused = True
    \
        \        if settings["notify_on_pause"]:
                notifications.append({"\
        after_event": row["id"], "recipient": "synthetic_owner"})
    return\
        \ {"trace": trace, "notifications": notifications,
            "simulated_work_seconds"\
        : sum(r.get("duration", 0) for r in trace if r["action"] == "run")}
\
        

def schedule_idle(data, settings):
    version, built, trace = 0, None,\
        \ []
    for row in data:
        if row["kind"] in settings["meaningful_inputs"\
        ]:
            version += 1
        if row["kind"] != "tick":
    \
        \        trace.append({"id": row["id"], "action": "input", "kind"\
        : row["kind"], "version": version})

        run\
        \ = not settings["suppress_unchanged_inputs"] or built != version
    \
        \    trace.append({**row, "version": version, "action": "run" if run\
        \ else "suppressed"})
        if run:
            built = version
  \
        \  return {"trace": trace, "simulated_work_seconds": sum(r.get("duration"\
        , 0) for r in trace if r["action"] == "run")}


def order_jobs(data,\
        \ settings):
    jobs = data["jobs"]
    preferred = set(data["previous_failures"\
        ])
    while True:
        expanded = preferred | {dep for job in jobs if\
        \ job["id"] in preferred for dep in job["needs"]}
        if expanded\
        \ == preferred:

        \ = []

        done, trace, clock, feedback\
        \ = {}, [], 0, None
        while len(done) < len(jobs):
            ready\
        \ = [job for job in jobs if job["id"] not in done and all(dep in done for\
        \ dep in job["needs"])]
            if not ready:
                raise\
        \ ValueError("Invalid replay dependency graph")
            if settings["\
        order"] == "previous_failure_ancestors_first":
                ready.sort(key=lambda\
        \ job: job["id"] not in preferred)
            job = ready[0]
       \
        \     skipped = any(done[dep] != "success" for dep in job["needs"])
\
        \            status = "skipped" if skipped else "failure" if job["id"\
        ] == case["failure"] else "success"
            started = clock
   \
        \         clock += 0 if skipped else job["duration"]
            if status\
        \ == "failure" and feedback is None:
                feedback = clock
\
        \            done[job["id"]] = status
            trace.append({"id"\
        : job["id"], "needs": job["needs"], "start": started, "end": clock,\
        \ "outcome": status})
        cases.append({"id": case["id"], "trace"\
        : trace, "first_failure_seconds": feedback,
                      "simulated_work_seconds"\
        : clock})
    return {"cases": cases, "simulated_work_seconds": sum(c["\
        simulated_work_seconds"] for c in cases)}


def queue_builds(data, settings):
\
        \    cases = {}
    for name, rows in data.items():
        pending, trace,\
        \ clock = list(rows), [], 0
        while pending:
            clock = max(clock,\
        \ min(row["arrival"] for row in pending))
            ready = [row for\
        \ row in pending if row["arrival"] <= clock]
            aged = [row for\
        \ row in ready if clock - row["arrival"] >= settings["max_wait"]]
  \
        \          reason = "fifo"
            if settings["order"] == "priority_with_aging"\
        :
                ready = aged if aged else ready
                reason\
        \ = "aging" if aged else "priority"
                ready.sort(key=lambda\
        \ row: (row["arrival"], rows.index(row)) if aged else
                \
        \           (-row["priority"], row["arrival"], rows.index(row)))
   \
        \         else:
                ready.sort(key=lambda row: (row["arrival"\
        ], rows.index(row)))
            row = ready[0]
            trace.append({**row,\
        \ "start": clock, "wait": clock - row["arrival"], "reason": reason})
\
        \            clock += row["duration"]
            pending.remove(row)
\
        \        cases[name] = {"trace": trace, "max_wait_seconds": max(row["\
        wait"] for row in trace),
                       "urgent_wait_seconds"\
        : next((row["wait"] for row in trace if row["id"] == "urgent"), None)}
\
        \    return {"cases": cases, "simulated_work_seconds": sum(r["duration"\
        ] for rows in data.values() for r in rows)}


def select_builds(data, settings):
\
        \    observed, trace, missed = None, [], []
    for row in data:
      \
        \  # Decision sees only the change and last executed build outcome.
    \
        \    run = not (settings["skip_docs_after_observed_success"] and row["\
        change"] == "docs" and observed == "success")
        trace.append({"\
        id": row["id"], "change": row["change"], "action": "run" if run\
        \ else "suppressed",
                      "last_observed_outcome": observed,
\
        \                      "observed_outcome": row["outcome"] if run else\
        \ None})
        if run:
            observed = row["outcome"]
     \
        \   elif row["outcome"] == "failure":
            missed.append({"id"\
        : row["id"], "cause": row.get("failure_cause")})  # Evaluator-only oracle.
\
        \    work = sum(row["duration"] for row, decision in zip(data, trace) if\
        \ decision["action"] == "run")
    return {"trace": trace, "missed_failures"\
        : len(missed), "missed_failure_details": missed,
            "missed_failure_rate"\
        : len(missed) / max(1, sum(r["outcome"] == "failure" for r in data)),

        \            "simulated_work_seconds": work, "simulated_saved_seconds"\
        : sum(r["duration"] for r in data) - work}


def predict_duration(data,\
        \ settings):
    history, trace = [], []
    for index, row in enumerate(data):
\
        \        pool = history
        if settings["predictor"] == "past_feature_mean"\
        :

        feature"]] or history

        \ r["actual"]) for r in held),

        \ sum(r["duration"] for r in data), "direct_speedup_claimed": False}
\
        

def run(pattern, settings, data):

        : schedule_failures, "P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE": schedule_idle,

        \    "P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST": order_jobs, "P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY": queue_builds,

        \               "P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT": select_builds, "P-LIT-DURATION-PREDICTION"\

'on':
  push:
    branches:
    - ct-scenario/**
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  probe:
    name: probe
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
    - name: Controlled workload
      shell: bash
      run: 'python3 - <<''CLOUDTUNE_REPLAY_ENGINE''

        import base64, zlib

        exec(compile(zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode('''')),
        ''scenario_replay.py'', ''exec''))

        CLOUDTUNE_REPLAY_ENGINE

        '
      env:
        CT_PATTERN: P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT
        CT_POLICY: '{"always_build": ["source", "lockfile", "setup"], "skip_docs_after_observed_success":
          false}'
        CT_DATA: '[{"change": "source", "duration": 5, "failure_cause": null, "id":
          0, "outcome": "success"}, {"change": "docs", "duration": 5, "failure_cause":
          null, "id": 1, "outcome": "success"}, {"change": "docs", "duration": 5,
          "failure_cause": "external_setup_failure", "id": 2, "outcome": "failure"},
          {"change": "lockfile", "duration": 5, "failure_cause": "build_failure",

          null, "id": 4, "outcome": "success"}, {"change": "setup", "duration": 5,
          "failure_cause": null, "id": 5, "outcome": "success"}, {"change": "docs",
          "duration": 5, "failure_cause": null, "id": 6, "outcome": "success"}, {"change":
          "source", "duration": 5, "failure_cause": "build_failure", "id": 7, "outcome":
          "failure"}]'

patterns.search_text:
Tune Bazel build parallelism

Pattern: P-LIT-BAZEL-PARALLEL (build_parallelism)

When is tune bazel build parallelism applicable?

Assess tune bazel build parallelism for this repository, preserve required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Existing Bazel build; Sufficient CPU and memory

Contraindications: Larger flags are assumed to supply more runner resources

Method: Compare concurrency within resource quotas; Keep targets and inputs identical

Reported finding: Long compilations benefited most from parallelism.

Reported metrics: {"long_build_median_speedup": {"cores_16": 12.8, "cores_2": 2, "cores_4": 3.84, "cores_8": 7.36}}

Source: Does Using Bazel Help Speed Up Continuous Integration Builds? (2024), 3.2.2; 4.2; 6.3; PDF pp. 18, 19, 31, 32, 33, 43: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.00796

Literature example before:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
build the same targets with one worker


Literature example after:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
build the same targets with an evaluated worker count

+++ knowledge/examples/P-LIT-BAZEL-PARALLEL/after.txt
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@

-build the same targets with one worker
+build the same targets with an evaluated worker count

Cache Bazel build results

Pattern: P-LIT-BAZEL-INCREMENTAL (incremental_build_cache)

When is cache bazel build results applicable?

Assess cache bazel build results for this repository, preserve required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Existing Bazel build; Trusted, input-keyed cache

Contraindications: Mutable undeclared inputs; Untrusted cache writes

Method: Separate dependency and result caching; Record cold behavior and hit rates

Reported finding: Result caching particularly helped long compilations.

Reported metrics: {"long_build_median_speedup": {"general_deps_and_results": 4.22, "specific_deps_and_results": 4.71}}

Source: Does Using Bazel Help Speed Up Continuous Integration Builds? (2024), 3.2.3; 4.3; Table 10; PDF pp. 24, 25, 36, 37, 38: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.00796

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.ruby == 'head' || matrix.gemfile == 'gemfiles/activerecord_edge.gemfile' }}
    env:
      DB: ${{ matrix.db }}
      BUNDLE_GEMFILE: ${{ matrix.gemfile }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        ruby:
          - '4.0'
          - 3.4
          - 3.3
        gemfile:
          - gemfiles/activerecord_edge.gemfile
          - gemfiles/activerecord_8.1.gemfile
          - gemfiles/activerecord_8.0.gemfile
        db:
          - mysql
          - postgresql
          - sqlite3
        include:
          - ruby: truffleruby-head
            db: postgresql
            gemfile: gemfiles/activerecord_8.0.gemfile

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:10
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: acts_as_taggable_on
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
        ports: ['5432:5432']
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      mysql:
        image: mysql:8
        env:
          MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD: true
        ports: ['3306:3306']
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "mysqladmin ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Set up Ruby
      uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: ${{ matrix.ruby }}
        bundler-cache: true
    - name: Cache Bundler dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: vendor/bundle
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-gems-${{ matrix.ruby }}-${{ matrix.gemfile }}-${{ hashFiles(matrix.gemfile) }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-gems-${{ matrix.ruby }}-${{ matrix.gemfile }}-\
          ${{ runner.os }}-gems-${{ matrix.ruby }}-\
          ${{ runner.os }}-gems-
    - name: Create MySQL test database with utf8mb4 charset
      if: ${{ matrix.db == 'mysql' }}
      run: |
        mysql -uroot --host=127.0.0.1 -e "CREATE DATABASE acts_as_taggable_on CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci"
    - name: Build and test with Rake
      run: |
        bundle exec rake
